A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a gene, tek, encoding an exported protein, which we have shown is processed to a 28-k Da protein.
we have cloned and sequenced the gene that encodes the 28 kDa extracellular protein of the pathogen, Pseudomonas Solanacearum, and have determined the function of the 28 kda protein.
we cloned and characterized the gene that encodes the 28-kD extracellular protein of the pathogen Pseudomonas Solanacearum, the causative agent of bacterial wilt of solanaceous crops.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tek is not essential for virulence.
the tek gene encodes a 28-kDal protein that is secreted by P. solacearum and that the tek gene is located on the same plasmid as the xpsR gene.
tek encodes the 58-kDa preprotein, which is processed extracellularly, to yield the 28-kD protein that is the most abundant of all of the P. solanaceaum extracellular proteins.
